cases.question: Investigate Spring's Kotlin KClass-based JDK proxy hint registration, from the convenience extensions through Java registration to the stored hints. Discover both the ProxyHints extension and the related JdkProxyHint.Builder extension, identify their Java handoffs, and explain argument order, duplicate arguments and fluent return values. Read the relevant Kotlin tests and explain what their mocked calls establish, without treating their example types as proof that real registration accepts those types. Trace the Java Class, TypeReference and consumer entry points, including fresh-builder creation, callback/build/insertion order and what a failed registration leaves behind. Explain which interface inputs are validated, how Class values become TypeReference values, and why the TypeReference route differs. Compare repeated builder additions, empty inputs, null elements, immutable hint construction and later builder changes. Describe the default reachable-type and Java-serialization metadata, how setters update it, and how it participates in hint equality and hashing. Finally explain registry deduplication and iteration order, including Class-backed versus name-backed references for the same type, reordered/repeated interfaces, changed metadata, and whole-hint deduplication versus merging interface lists. Assume non-null KClass/Class elements, vararg arrays and callbacks, well-formed type names, and the built-in TypeReference factories; custom TypeReference implementations are outside scope. The one null-input case to analyze is a non-null TypeReference array containing a null element: describe the Java implementation's behavior despite the non-null API contract. Consumers only configure their supplied builder; exclude nested registration and unrelated callback side effects. This task concerns storing hints, not creating proxies: exclude AOP interface completion, native-image output, classloader/condition evaluation and detailed type-name parsing. Do not execute repository code, tests or builds. Use one contiguous representative verbatim quote of at most 40 physical lines per finding; explain separately inspected helpers or tests in prose rather than stitching excerpts. No source paths or line locations are supplied: locate the implementations yourself.

findings.description: Trace both KClass extensions to the corresponding Class-varargs Java members, preserving argument sequence and fluent receiver returns. Explain the limitation of the mocked Kotlin tests. Use the ProxyHints Kotlin extension as the representative citation.

Trace the Class and TypeReference registration overloads through the consumer form, then fresh builder, callback, build, insertion and fluent return. Explain propagation and absence of a new stored hint when configuration/build fails. Use the consumer registration body as the representative citation.

Explain non-sealed-interface validation, its failure type and timing before appending, and the Class-to-TypeReference conversion helper chain. Contrast direct TypeReference registration, including references to unavailable or non-interface types. Use the Class-validation helper as the representative citation.

Explain ordered append behavior across builder calls, repeated interfaces, empty inputs and an empty completed hint. Explain the immutable interface-list snapshot, later builder mutation, and the delayed failure for a null TypeReference element. Use completed-hint construction as the representative citation.

Explain default reachable-type/serialization state, fluent setters and snapshotting, then equality's ordered interface list and metadata fields. Distinguish equality from the narrower hash computation and explain metadata-only hash collisions. Use the hint equals/hashCode implementation as the representative citation.

Explain first-unique-insertion registry order and duplicate suppression using completed-hint equality, not sorting or merging interface lists. Trace built-in TypeReference equality/hash behavior so equivalent Class-backed and name-backed references can deduplicate. Use registry storage and stream exposure as the representative citation.
